answer: Each agent can open a payment channel only after locking a scarce deposit, then earns a reputation score from counterparties who risk their own funds on completed trades. The trellis of channels may spread across a meadow of newcomers, but a ridge of costly deposits limits how many identities one attacker can activate at once. Sybils therefore require tying up real capital, and dishonest trades can forfeit it; creating names alone buys no influence.
